The design review of 1 Aug scored information architecture at 4/10 for one reason: twenty-one screens existed with no shell and no routing between them. This document is that shell.

## 1. The decision

**No tab bar.** Today is the only root. Everything else is reached from a single `≡` in the Today header, which opens a full-screen menu.

Rejected alternative: a three-tab bar (Today / History / You) with a capture FAB. It is the conventional answer and it was rejected because four of the eight destinations below are visited less than weekly, and a permanent 83pt bar spends the most valuable screen real estate in the app on navigation that is mostly idle. The ring is the product; it gets the room.

The cost of dropping the tab bar is that capture loses its permanent affordance. That is bought back by pinning **＋ Log food** to the bottom of the menu as well as the home screen, so capture is at most two taps from anywhere in the app and one tap from the place users spend 90% of their time.

## 2. Two rules

1. **Today is the only root.** Every non-modal screen is a push off Today and its back gesture returns there (or to the screen that pushed it, where that is unambiguous).
2. **Only two things are modal.** Capture, and the pre-session stack (auth + onboarding). A modal owns the whole viewport, has no `≡`, and dismissing it always lands on Today.

Everything else follows from these.

## 3. Routing table

| Screen | Kind | Reached from | Back goes to |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| Today | root | App launch; dismissing any modal | Nothing — it is the root |
| Menu | overlay | `≡` in the Today header | Today (✕ or backdrop) |
| Calendar picker | sheet | Tapping the date title on Today | Today, on the day picked |
| What should I eat? | sheet | The suggestion row on Today | Today |
| Entry detail | push | An entry row on Today; a day in History | Wherever it was opened from |
| History | push | Menu › History | Today |
| Week detail | push | A week card in History | History |
| Streak | push | Menu › Streak; the streak chip on Today | Today |
| Recap | push | Menu › Recap; the morning notification | Today |
| Targets · Target history | push | Menu › Targets; Settings › Targets | Today |
| Settings · Account · Delete account | push | Menu › Settings, Menu › Account | Today |
| Capture → Analyzing → Review → Saved | modal | ＋ Log food, on Today and in the Menu | ✕ drops the whole stack → Today |
| Welcome · Register · Verify · Reset | modal | No valid session | Only forward, or out of the app |
| Onboarding Q1–10 → Building → Targets | modal | First session after registering | One question at a time; no exit |

## 4. The menu

Eight rows, each carrying its own current state so the menu doubles as a status readout rather than a list of nouns:

| Row | Trailing state |
| -- | -- |
| Today | today's calories |
| History | days logged, all time |
| Streak | current · best |
| Last night's recap | `NEW` when unread |
| Targets | current calorie / protein target |
| Settings | — |
| Account | account name |
| Help & feedback | — |

Header carries the account name and the date logging started. Footer is pinned **＋ Log food**.

## 5. Implementation notes

* One native stack navigator with Today as the only root route. The menu is a route presented modally over it, not a drawer — a drawer implies a swipe-from-edge gesture we do not want competing with future swipe-between-days.
* The capture stack and the pre-session stack are separate navigators presented modally, so their internal back behaviour cannot leak into the main stack.
* Deep links (from the morning recap notification) push onto Today rather than replacing it, so the back gesture always has somewhere to go.
* Week detail is specified here but not yet designed. It should be a weekly form of the recap in doc 17.
